title: Attackers and defenders
summary: When a piece is defended, count. And start the exchange with your cheapest piece.

steps.title: Counting an exchange
steps.text:
A defended piece can still be won. The question changes from *is it loose?* to *who runs out of recaptures first?*

Count the attackers. Count the defenders. If you have more attackers, and your first capture doesn't hand back more than it takes, you win something.

Here the bishop on @e5 is attacked twice, by the knight on @f3 and the rook on @e1. It is defended once, by the knight on @d7.

ask.question: Play it out in your head: Nx@e5 Nx@e5 Rx@e5. Who is ahead at the end?
ask.answer: @W. @W took a bishop and a knight (6) and gave a knight (3). A clean bishop up.

steps.explain: The knight on @f3 and the rook on @e1. The bishop on @c1 stands on the same colour as @e5 but on a different diagonal, so it doesn't count.

steps.prompt: Now tap every @B piece that defends @e5.
steps.explain: Only the knight on @d7. Two attackers against one defender.

steps.prompt: In one of these positions Nx@e5 wins a piece. In the other it is just a trade.
steps.question: In the other position, why is Nx@e5 only a trade?

choices.text: The rook is on @a1, no longer on the file that leads to @e5. Now it is one attacker against one defender.
The bishop on @e5 is loose there.

steps.explain: Same bishop, same defender. What changed is the count: take away the second attacker and Nx@e5 Nx@e5 ends the sequence with nothing gained.

steps.prompt: The knight on @d5 is attacked twice, by the knight on @c3 and the queen on @d1. It is defended once, by the rook on @a5.
steps.question: Which capture should come first?

choices.text: Nx@d5. Start with the cheaper piece. If the rook takes back, the queen takes the rook.
Qx@d5. The queen is the strongest attacker, so it should lead.
Either one. Two attackers beat one defender, whatever the order.

steps.explain: Counting heads is not enough; you also count values. Qx@d5 Rx@d5 Nx@d5 gives a queen (9) for a knight and a rook (8). Nx@d5 first risks only a knight.
